intro: Pack your bags! Today you learn the words you need at the airport, at the hotel and when you buy a ticket, how to describe a route with into, across, along and past, and how to say what you do on holiday. Warm-up: where do you like going on holiday?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in small themed groups with an Indonesian gloss and practise them in short sentences, not only as translations. Airport: passport, flight, check in (verb, two words) / the check-in desk (noun), boarding pass (British also 'boarding card'), gate, luggage / baggage, delay / delayed. Hotel: book a room (book = memesan as a verb), reservation (also 'booking'), single room (one person), double room (two people, one big bed; a twin room has two single beds), reception, check in / check out. Tickets: one-way ticket, return ticket (British) = round-trip ticket (American); British people also say 'a single' for a one-way ticket.

Airport and hotel traps. Indonesians say 'pesawatnya delay', using delay like an adjective: in English it's 'The flight is delayed' or 'There's a delay' (never 'The flight is delay'). Luggage and baggage are uncountable, like rice and water from A1: no a/an, no -s (*'two luggages' → two bags / two suitcases / some luggage). 'Resepsionis' is the person (receptionist); the desk is 'reception'. Don't teach 'a piece of luggage' unless asked.

Prepositions of movement: into (masuk ke dalam) / out of (keluar dari), across (from one side to the other: across the road, across the bridge), along (following a road, river or beach), past (go by something without stopping or going in). The most common error is *'Walk pass the bank': pass and past sound almost the same; pass is a verb on its own (You pass the bank), past is the little word after walk / go / drive (Walk past the bank). Into is movement, in is position (Go into the station / I'm in the station). 'Cross the road' (A1) = 'go across the road'.

Vehicles: get on / get off a bus, train, plane, boat, motorbike or bike (big vehicles you can stand up in, or ones you sit on top of); get into / get out of a car or taxi (small: you bend down and sit). Accept get in / get out (of). Indonesian naik / turun covers all of them, which gives *'We go into the bus' → We get on the bus. Keep 'by bus' (how you travel, from A1) separate from 'get on the bus' (the moment you step in).

Holidays: go on holiday (pergi liburan; never *'go to holiday'), be on holiday (sedang liburan), go to + a place (go to Lombok), go + -ing for activities (go sightseeing, go snorkelling, go swimming, from A1 hobbies), take photos (not *'make photos'), buy souvenirs, stay at a hotel. Holiday (British) = vacation (American); snorkelling (British) = snorkeling (American). Indonesian 'jalan-jalan' can be go sightseeing, go for a walk or travel: choose by meaning.

Limits: A1 grammar only: present simple and continuous, imperatives, can, there is/are, like + -ing, I'd like (and the chunk 'I'd like to check out'). No past simple, no will or going to, no present perfect: talk about holidays as habits (Every year we go…) or what's happening now (We're on holiday in Bali. Today we're at the beach.). Don't teach through, over, towards, up/down, other phrasal verbs, or the present continuous for future plans.

keyPoints.title: Airport, hotel and ticket words
keyPoints.explanation: Airport: passport, flight, check in, boarding pass, gate, luggage / baggage (uncountable: no a, no -s), delay / delayed. Hotel: book a room, reservation, single room, double room, reception, check out. Tickets: one-way ticket, return ticket (British) = round-trip ticket (American). Say 'The flight is delayed', not 'The flight is delay'.

examples.en: Can I see your passport, please?
I have a reservation for a double room.
examples.id: Saya punya reservasi untuk kamar double.

id.title: Kosakata bandara, hotel dan tiket
id.explanation: Bandara: passport (paspor), flight (penerbangan), check in (lapor diri / check-in), boarding pass (kartu naik pesawat), gate (pintu keberangkatan), luggage / baggage (bagasi, barang bawaan; tidak bisa dihitung: tanpa a, tanpa -s), delay / delayed (penundaan / ditunda). Hotel: book a room (memesan kamar), reservation (reservasi), single room (kamar untuk satu orang), double room (kamar untuk dua orang), reception (meja resepsionis), check out (keluar dari hotel). Tiket: one-way ticket (sekali jalan), return ticket (UK) = round-trip ticket (US) (pulang-pergi). Katakan 'The flight is delayed', bukan 'The flight is delay'.

keyPoints.title: Prepositions of movement
keyPoints.explanation: into / out of (go in / come out), across (from one side to the other), along (following a road, river or beach), past (go by without stopping). Walk past the bank, not 'walk pass'. Get on / get off a bus, train, plane or motorbike; get into / get out of a car or taxi.

examples.en: Walk along the river and go across the bridge.
examples.id: Jalan menyusuri sungai lalu seberangi jembatannya.

examples.en: Go past the mosque. The hotel is on the left.
examples.id: Lewati masjidnya. Hotelnya di sebelah kiri.

examples.en: Get on the bus at the bus stop.

id.title: Preposisi gerak
id.explanation: into / out of (masuk ke dalam / keluar dari), across (menyeberangi, dari satu sisi ke sisi lain), along (menyusuri jalan, sungai atau pantai), past (melewati tanpa berhenti). Walk past the bank, bukan 'walk pass'. Get on / get off untuk bus, kereta, pesawat atau motor; get into / get out of untuk mobil atau taksi.

keyPoints.title: Holiday activities
keyPoints.explanation: Go on holiday (not 'go to holiday'), be on holiday, go to + a place. Activities: go sightseeing, go snorkelling, go swimming, take photos, buy souvenirs, stay at a hotel. Holiday (British) = vacation (American).

examples.en: Every year we go on holiday to Lombok.
examples.id: Setiap tahun kami pergi liburan ke Lombok.

examples.en: I like going snorkelling in Labuan Bajo.
examples.id: Saya suka snorkeling di Labuan Bajo.

examples.en: Dimas is on holiday in Bali. He's taking photos at the beach.
examples.id: Dimas sedang liburan di Bali. Dia sedang foto-foto di pantai.

id.title: Kegiatan liburan
id.explanation: Go on holiday (pergi liburan; bukan 'go to holiday'), be on holiday (sedang liburan), go to + tempat (go to Lombok). Kegiatan: go sightseeing (jalan-jalan melihat tempat wisata), go snorkelling (snorkeling), go swimming (berenang), take photos (foto-foto), buy souvenirs (beli suvenir / oleh-oleh), stay at a hotel (menginap di hotel). Holiday (UK) = vacation (US).

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: I have two luggages.
expected: i have two pieces of luggage
guidedPractice.hint: Luggage has no -s and no a. Count the bags or suitcases (koper).

guidedPractice.prompt: You go from Jakarta to Bandung by train and you come back to Jakarta in the evening. Complete with one word: A ___ ticket to Bandung, please.
guidedPractice.hint: Tiket pulang-pergi. British and American English use different words.

guidedPractice.prompt: The hotel is on the other side of the river. Complete with one word: Go ___ the bridge and the hotel is on the right.
guidedPractice.hint: From one side to the other side.

guidedPractice.prompt: The bus is at the bus stop and the doors open. Complete with one word: Rina gets ___ the bus.
guidedPractice.hint: A bus is big: you can stand up and walk in it.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Sari goes to holiday every December.
expected: sari goes on holiday every december
every december sari goes on holiday

independentPractice.prompt: You arrive at a hotel in Bali with your booking. Where do you go first? (one word)
independentPractice.hint: The desk where the receptionist works.

independentPractice.prompt: Translate into English: Jalan kaki menyusuri pantai sampai ke hotel.
expected: walk along the beach to the hotel
go along the beach to the hotel
walk along the beach to get to the hotel
independentPractice.hint: Menyusuri = following the beach from one end to the other.

independentPractice.prompt: What do you like doing on holiday? Write one sentence with I like + -ing.
independentPractice.hint: For example: going sightseeing, taking photos, going snorkelling.

assessment.prompt: Complete with two words: At the check-in desk at Soekarno-Hatta, you show your passport and the airline gives you a ___ ___. You need it at the gate.
assessment.rubric: Correct: boarding pass (British 'boarding card' is also fine). 'plane ticket' / 'flight ticket' = 0 (you buy the ticket before, the boarding pass comes at check-in). Small spelling slip (bording pass) = 80.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: Our plane to Lombok can't leave at 9:00 because of bad weather. There's a two-hour ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: delay (after 'a' you need the noun). 'delayed' = 50 (right idea, wrong form). 'late' = 0 (not after 'a two-hour').

assessment.prompt: You're at a hotel in Labuan Bajo. You are alone, so you need a room for one person. Complete with one word: Can I book a ___ room for two nights, please?
assessment.rubric: Correct: single. 'double' or 'twin' = 0 (those are rooms for two people). 'one' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Drive pass the school and stop at the hotel.
acceptableAnswers: drive past the school and stop at the hotel
drive by the school and stop at the hotel
pass the school and stop at the hotel
assessment.rubric: Correct: Drive past the school… (past after drive / walk / go). 'Pass the school and stop…' (pass as the verb, without 'drive') is also correct. Any sentence still with 'drive pass' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: The taxi is here. Pak Hasan opens the door and gets ___ the taxi.
assessment.rubric: Correct: into (or in). 'on' = 0 (on is for a bus, train, plane or motorbike). 'to' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: In Yogyakarta we go ___. We visit Borobudur, Prambanan and the Kraton.
assessment.rubric: Correct: sightseeing (go + -ing = visit famous places). Small spelling slip (sight-seeing, sightseing) = 80. 'shopping' or 'swimming' = 0 (doesn't match the visits).

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: Budi has a new camera. On holiday in Lombok he ___ a lot of photos.
assessment.rubric: Correct: takes (take photos; he → -s). 'take' = 60 (right word, missing -s). 'makes' = 0 (not 'make photos').

blocks.text:
Your trip from **Soekarno-Hatta** to **Ngurah Rai** (Bali), step by step:
- Bring your **passport** (paspor) or ID card and look for your **flight** (penerbangan), for example *GA 404 to Denpasar*.
- **Check in** (lapor diri) at the **check-in desk**: you give them your **luggage** or **baggage** (bagasi, barang bawaan) and they give you a **boarding pass** (kartu naik pesawat).
- Go to the **gate** (pintu keberangkatan), for example *gate 7*, and get on the plane.
- Sometimes the plane is late: there's a **delay** (penundaan) and the flight is **delayed** (ditunda).

**Check in** is the action (two words: *We check in at 6.*); **check-in** with a dash is the desk or the time (*the check-in desk*).

id.text:
Perjalananmu dari **Soekarno-Hatta** ke **Ngurah Rai** (Bali), langkah demi langkah:
- Bawa **passport** (paspor) atau KTP dan cari **flight** (penerbangan) kamu, misalnya *GA 404 to Denpasar*.
- **Check in** (lapor diri) di **check-in desk** (meja check-in): kamu menyerahkan **luggage** atau **baggage** (bagasi, barang bawaan) dan mereka memberimu **boarding pass** (kartu naik pesawat).
- Pergi ke **gate** (pintu keberangkatan), misalnya *gate 7*, lalu naik ke pesawat.
- Kadang pesawatnya terlambat: ada **delay** (penundaan) dan penerbangannya **delayed** (ditunda).

**Check in** adalah tindakannya (dua kata: *We check in at 6.* = Kami check-in jam 6.); **check-in** dengan tanda hubung adalah mejanya atau waktunya (*the check-in desk*).

rows.en: Can I see your passport, please?
rows.id: Boleh saya lihat paspor Anda?

rows.en: We check in two hours before the flight.
rows.id: Kami check-in dua jam sebelum penerbangan.

rows.en: I have one bag and a small suitcase.
rows.id: Saya bawa satu tas dan satu koper kecil.
rows.note: suitcase = koper; you can count bags and suitcases

id.note: suitcase = koper; tas dan koper bisa dihitung

rows.en: Flight GA 404 is boarding at gate 7.
rows.id: Penumpang GA 404 dipersilakan naik di gate 7.
rows.note: boarding = passengers are getting on the plane now

id.note: boarding = penumpang sedang naik ke pesawat sekarang

rows.en: Sorry, the flight to Ngurah Rai is delayed.
rows.id: Maaf, penerbangan ke Ngurah Rai ditunda.

blocks.text:
**'Pesawatnya delay'** is Indonesian. In English *delay* is a thing (a noun): **There's a delay.** To describe the flight, add **is** and **-ed**: **The flight is delayed.** Never 'The flight is delay'.

**Luggage** and **baggage** can't be counted, like *rice* and *water* (you know them from A1): no *a*, no *-s*. Say **some luggage**, **my luggage**, never 'two luggages'. To count, count the **bags** or **suitcases**: *I have two bags.*

British and American English: both use **luggage** and **baggage**; airports often say *baggage*. British people also say **boarding card** for boarding pass.

id.text:
**'Pesawatnya delay'** itu bahasa Indonesia. Dalam bahasa Inggris *delay* adalah sebuah benda (kata benda): **There's a delay.** (Ada penundaan.) Untuk menjelaskan penerbangannya, tambahkan **is** dan **-ed**: **The flight is delayed.** Jangan 'The flight is delay'.

**Luggage** dan **baggage** tidak bisa dihitung, seperti *rice* dan *water* (sudah kamu kenal di A1): tanpa *a*, tanpa *-s*. Katakan **some luggage**, **my luggage**, jangan 'two luggages'. Untuk menghitung, hitung **bags** (tas) atau **suitcases** (koper)-nya: *I have two bags.*

Inggris (UK) dan Amerika (US): keduanya memakai **luggage** dan **baggage**; di bandara sering tertulis *baggage*. Orang Inggris juga bilang **boarding card** untuk boarding pass.

blocks.prompt: The screen at the airport says: GA 410 LOMBOK — DELAYED. What does it mean?
options: The plane to Lombok leaves late.
The plane to Lombok leaves early.
The plane to Lombok is at the gate now.
blocks.explain: Delayed = ditunda: the plane leaves later than the time on your ticket.

id.prompt: Layar di bandara bertuliskan: GA 410 LOMBOK — DELAYED. Apa artinya?
id.explain: Delayed = ditunda: pesawatnya berangkat lebih lambat dari jam di tiketmu.

blocks.text:
**At the hotel:**
- **book a room** = memesan kamar. *Can I book a room for two nights?* Your booking is a **reservation** (also *booking*).
- **single room** = for one person; **double room** = for two people, with one big bed.
- **reception** = meja resepsionis, the desk at the entrance. You **check in** when you arrive and **check out** when you leave and pay.

**Tickets** for the train, bus, plane or boat:
- **one-way ticket** = sekali jalan (you go, you don't come back).
- **return ticket** = pulang-pergi (you go and you come back).

id.text:
**Di hotel:**
- **book a room** = memesan kamar. *Can I book a room for two nights?* (Bisa saya pesan kamar untuk dua malam?) Pesananmu disebut **reservation** (reservasi, juga *booking*).
- **single room** = untuk satu orang; **double room** = untuk dua orang, dengan satu ranjang besar.
- **reception** = meja resepsionis, meja di dekat pintu masuk. Kamu **check in** saat datang dan **check out** saat pergi dan membayar.

**Tiket** kereta, bus, pesawat atau kapal:
- **one-way ticket** = sekali jalan (pergi saja, tidak kembali).
- **return ticket** = pulang-pergi (pergi lalu kembali).

rows.en: Good afternoon. I have a reservation. My name is Budi Santoso.
rows.id: Selamat sore. Saya sudah reservasi. Nama saya Budi Santoso.

rows.en: We'd like a double room, please.
rows.id: Kami mau kamar double.

rows.en: Check-out is at 12 noon.
rows.id: Check-out jam 12 siang.

rows.en: A one-way ticket to Surabaya, please.
rows.id: Satu tiket sekali jalan ke Surabaya.

rows.en: A return ticket to Lombok costs 1,800,000 rupiah.
rows.id: Tiket pulang-pergi ke Lombok harganya 1.800.000 rupiah.

blocks.text:
**Reception or receptionist?** In Indonesian, *resepsionis* is the person. In English the person is the **receptionist**, and the desk is **reception**: *Ask at reception.*

**Book** is also a verb: **book a room** = memesan kamar (not buku!).

**Two beds?** A **double room** has one big bed. A room with two small beds is a **twin room**: you see it on booking apps.

**Return** usually means 'kembali', but **a return ticket** is a ticket there **and** back. British and American English: **return ticket** (UK) = **round-trip ticket** (US). British people also say **a single** for a one-way ticket. Don't mix it up with a **single room** (for one person)!

id.text:
**Reception atau receptionist?** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *resepsionis* adalah orangnya. Dalam bahasa Inggris orangnya **receptionist**, dan mejanya **reception**: *Ask at reception.* (Tanya di meja resepsionis.)

**Book** juga kata kerja: **book a room** = memesan kamar (bukan buku!).

**Dua ranjang?** **Double room** punya satu ranjang besar. Kamar dengan dua ranjang kecil disebut **twin room**: kamu sering melihatnya di aplikasi pemesanan.

**Return** biasanya berarti 'kembali', tapi **a return ticket** adalah tiket pergi **dan** pulang. Inggris (UK) dan Amerika (US): **return ticket** (UK) = **round-trip ticket** (US). Orang Inggris juga bilang **a single** untuk tiket sekali jalan. Jangan tertukar dengan **single room** (kamar untuk satu orang)!

blocks.prompt: It's your last day at the hotel. You want to pay and leave. What do you say at reception?
options: I'd like to check in, please.
I'd like to check out, please.
blocks.explain: You check out when you leave and pay. You check in when you arrive. A reservation is what you make before you come.

id.prompt: Ini hari terakhirmu di hotel. Kamu mau membayar dan pergi. Apa yang kamu katakan di meja resepsionis?
id.explain: Check out saat kamu pergi dan membayar. Check in saat kamu datang. Reservation adalah pesanan yang kamu buat sebelum datang.

blocks.text:
These little words (**prepositions of movement**, kata depan untuk gerakan) say **where you move**. They come after a moving verb like *go, walk, drive, run*.
- **into** = masuk ke dalam: *Go into the station.*
- **out of** = keluar dari: *Come out of the hotel.*
- **across** = menyeberangi, from one side to the other side: *Walk across the road.*
- **along** = menyusuri, sepanjang (a road, a river, a beach): *Walk along the beach.*
- **past** = melewati, you go by it and don't stop: *Go past the mosque.*

Use them in directions with what you know from A1: *Turn left. Go past the bank. The hotel is on the right.*

id.text:
Kata-kata kecil ini (**prepositions of movement**, kata depan untuk gerakan) menjelaskan **ke mana kamu bergerak**. Letaknya setelah kata kerja gerak seperti *go, walk, drive, run* (pergi, berjalan, menyetir, berlari).
- **into** = masuk ke dalam: *Go into the station.*
- **out of** = keluar dari: *Come out of the hotel.*
- **across** = menyeberangi, dari satu sisi ke sisi lain: *Walk across the road.*
- **along** = menyusuri, sepanjang (jalan, sungai, pantai): *Walk along the beach.*
- **past** = melewati, kamu lewat dan tidak berhenti: *Go past the mosque.*

Pakai dalam petunjuk arah dengan yang sudah kamu tahu dari A1: *Turn left. Go past the bank. The hotel is on the right.*

rows.en: Walk along this road to the traffic lights.
rows.id: Jalan menyusuri jalan ini sampai lampu merah.

rows.en: Go across the bridge. The market is on the left.
rows.id: Seberangi jembatannya. Pasarnya di sebelah kiri.

rows.en: Walk past the mosque and turn right.
rows.id: Lewati masjidnya lalu belok kanan.

rows.en: The children are running into the sea.
rows.id: Anak-anak sedang berlari masuk ke laut.

rows.en: A lot of people are coming out of the station.
rows.id: Banyak orang sedang keluar dari stasiun.

blocks.text:
**Pass or past?** They sound almost the same, so people often write *'walk pass the bank'*. But they're different words:
- **pass** is an action on its own (a verb): *You **pass** the bank.*
- **past** is the little word after *walk / go / drive*: *Walk **past** the bank.*
So: **walk past**, **go past**, **drive past**, never 'walk pass'.

**In or into?** **into** is for movement (*Go **into** the hotel.*), **in** is for where something is (*I'm **in** the hotel.*). Indonesian *masuk ke* = **into**.

**Cross the road** (from A1) = **go across the road**: the same meaning.

id.text:
**Pass atau past?** Bunyinya hampir sama, jadi orang sering menulis *'walk pass the bank'*. Padahal kata ini berbeda:
- **pass** adalah tindakan yang berdiri sendiri (kata kerja): *You **pass** the bank.* (Kamu melewati bank.)
- **past** adalah kata kecil setelah *walk / go / drive*: *Walk **past** the bank.*
Jadi: **walk past**, **go past**, **drive past**, jangan 'walk pass'.

**In atau into?** **into** untuk gerakan (*Go **into** the hotel.* = Masuk ke hotel.), **in** untuk letak (*I'm **in** the hotel.* = Saya di dalam hotel.). *Masuk ke* = **into**.

**Cross the road** (dari A1) = **go across the road**: artinya sama.

blocks.prompt: Rina walks next to the sea, from one end of the beach to the other end. Choose the best word: Rina walks ___ the beach.
blocks.explain: Along = following the beach from one end to the other (menyusuri). Across goes from one side to the other side (from the road to the sea), and into means going inside something.

id.prompt: Rina berjalan di dekat laut, dari ujung pantai ke ujung yang lain. Pilih kata yang paling tepat: Rina walks ___ the beach.
id.explain: Along = mengikuti pantai dari satu ujung ke ujung lain (menyusuri). Across dari satu sisi ke sisi seberang (dari jalan ke laut), dan into berarti masuk ke dalam sesuatu.

material.title: Get on the bus, get into the taxi

blocks.text:
Indonesian uses **naik** and **turun** for every vehicle. English uses two pairs:
- **get on / get off**: a **bus**, **train**, **plane**, **boat**, **motorbike** or **bike**. These are big (you can stand up and walk inside) or you sit on top of them.
- **get into / get out of**: a **car** or **taxi**. These are small: you bend down and sit inside. (*get in / get out* is fine too.)

Don't mix this with A1 **by bus** (naik bus = how you travel: *I go to work by bus*). **Get on the bus** is the moment you step in.

id.text:
Bahasa Indonesia memakai **naik** dan **turun** untuk semua kendaraan. Bahasa Inggris memakai dua pasang kata:
- **get on / get off**: **bus**, **train** (kereta), **plane** (pesawat), **boat** (kapal), **motorbike** (motor) atau **bike** (sepeda). Kendaraan ini besar (kamu bisa berdiri dan berjalan di dalamnya) atau kamu duduk di atasnya.
- **get into / get out of**: **car** (mobil) atau **taxi**. Kendaraan ini kecil: kamu membungkuk lalu duduk di dalamnya. (*get in / get out* juga boleh.)

Jangan dicampur dengan **by bus** dari A1 (naik bus = cara bepergian: *I go to work by bus*). **Get on the bus** adalah saat kamu melangkah masuk ke bus.

rows.en: The bus is here. Let's get on!
rows.id: Busnya datang. Ayo naik!

rows.en: We get off the plane at Ngurah Rai Airport.
rows.id: Kami turun dari pesawat di Bandara Ngurah Rai.

rows.en: The ojek is here. I get on the motorbike.
rows.id: Ojeknya sudah datang. Saya naik ke motornya.

rows.en: Get into the car, please.
rows.id: Silakan masuk ke mobil.

rows.en: Sari gets out of the taxi at the hotel.
rows.id: Sari turun dari taksi di hotel.

blocks.text:
**'We go into the bus'** is a word-for-word guess. Say **We get on the bus.** The opposite is **get off**: *We get off the bus at the market.*

For a car or taxi it's **into / out of**: *Get into the taxi.* Not 'get on the taxi'.

Quick test: can you stand up inside, or do you sit on top? → **on / off**. Do you bend down and sit inside? → **into / out of**.

id.text:
**'We go into the bus'** adalah terjemahan kata per kata. Katakan **We get on the bus.** Lawannya **get off**: *We get off the bus at the market.* (Kami turun dari bus di pasar.)

Untuk mobil atau taksi pakai **into / out of**: *Get into the taxi.* Bukan 'get on the taxi'.

Tes cepat: bisa berdiri di dalamnya, atau duduk di atasnya? → **on / off**. Harus membungkuk lalu duduk di dalam? → **into / out of**.

blocks.prompt: Budi is in a Grab car. Now he is at his office. What does he do?
options: He gets out of the car.
blocks.explain: A car is small, so it's get into / get out of. 'Gets off' is for a bus, train or motorbike, and 'gets out the car' needs 'of'.

id.prompt: Budi naik mobil Grab. Sekarang dia sudah sampai di kantornya. Apa yang dia lakukan?
id.explain: Mobil itu kecil, jadi pakai get into / get out of. 'Gets off' untuk bus, kereta atau motor, dan 'gets out the car' kurang 'of'.

blocks.text:
Three patterns with **go**:
- **go on holiday** = pergi liburan: *We go on holiday in July.* When you're there, you're **on holiday** (sedang liburan).
- **go to** + a place: *go to Lombok, go to the beach.*
- **go** + **-ing** for activities (you know *go swimming* from A1): **go sightseeing** (jalan-jalan melihat tempat wisata), **go snorkelling** (snorkeling), **go swimming**.

More holiday words: **take photos** (foto-foto), **buy souvenirs** (beli suvenir, oleh-oleh), **stay at a hotel** (menginap di hotel), **visit a temple** (mengunjungi candi / pura).

id.text:
Tiga pola dengan **go**:
- **go on holiday** = pergi liburan: *We go on holiday in July.* Saat kamu di sana, kamu **on holiday** (sedang liburan).
- **go to** + tempat: *go to Lombok, go to the beach* (ke pantai).
- **go** + **-ing** untuk kegiatan (kamu sudah kenal *go swimming* dari A1): **go sightseeing** (jalan-jalan melihat tempat wisata), **go snorkelling** (snorkeling), **go swimming** (berenang).

Kata liburan lainnya: **take photos** (foto-foto), **buy souvenirs** (beli suvenir, oleh-oleh), **stay at a hotel** (menginap di hotel), **visit a temple** (mengunjungi candi / pura).

rows.en: Every December my family goes on holiday to Labuan Bajo.
rows.id: Setiap Desember keluarga saya pergi liburan ke Labuan Bajo.

rows.en: We stay at a small hotel near the beach.
rows.id: Kami menginap di hotel kecil dekat pantai.

rows.en: My brother likes going snorkelling, and I like taking photos.
rows.id: Adik saya suka snorkeling, dan saya suka foto-foto.

rows.en: Today we're in Bali. We're visiting a temple in Ubud.
rows.id: Hari ini kami di Bali. Kami sedang mengunjungi pura di Ubud.

rows.en: I'd like to buy some souvenirs for my friends.
rows.id: Saya mau beli oleh-oleh untuk teman-teman saya.

blocks.text:
**'Go to holiday'** is wrong: holiday is not a place. Say **go on holiday**. But a place takes **to**: *go to Bali*. Both together: *We go on holiday to Bali.*

**Take photos**, not 'make photos'. *Take* is like *ambil*: ambil foto.

**Jalan-jalan** has many meanings: to visit famous places it's **go sightseeing**; for a short walk it's **go for a walk**.

British and American English: **holiday** (UK) = **vacation** (US); **snorkelling** (UK) = **snorkeling** (US, one l).

id.text:
**'Go to holiday'** itu salah: holiday bukan tempat. Katakan **go on holiday**. Tapi tempat memakai **to**: *go to Bali*. Digabung: *We go on holiday to Bali.*

**Take photos**, bukan 'make photos'. *Take* itu seperti *ambil*: ambil foto.

**Jalan-jalan** punya banyak arti: untuk melihat tempat wisata pakai **go sightseeing**; untuk jalan kaki sebentar pakai **go for a walk**.

Inggris (UK) dan Amerika (US): **holiday** (UK) = **vacation** (US); **snorkelling** (UK) = **snorkeling** (US, satu huruf l).

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means 'Kami sedang liburan di Bali'?
options: We are in holiday in Bali.

blocks.explain: Sedang liburan = be on holiday: We are on holiday. 'In holiday' and 'go to holiday' are wrong, because holiday takes on.

id.explain: Sedang liburan = be on holiday: We are on holiday. 'In holiday' dan 'go to holiday' salah, karena holiday memakai on.
